channel.title: Matthew Collaro — Writing
channel.description: Essays on model-based systems engineering by Matthew Collaro.

item.title: Why Requirements Traceability Breaks, and What Actually Fixes It — Matthew Collaro
item.description: Traceability decays on real programs for structural reasons, not because engineers are lazy. A look at the actual failure modes and what a fix has to do.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: Model Governance for SysML Programs That Have to Certify — Matthew Collaro
item.description: When the model is the certification artifact rather than a picture of one, governance stops being bureaucracy and becomes the thing that makes the model trustworthy.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: Interface Control Documents Should Be Models — Matthew Collaro
item.description: The ICD is where integration problems are born. Treating it as a document instead of a model is why interfaces that pass review still fail on the bench.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: Guardrails for AI-Generated Engineering Artifacts — Matthew Collaro
item.description: Reviewing generated requirements and models by reading them does not scale and does not work. The check has to be structural, and the generator must not be able to route around it.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: Model Context Protocol for Engineering Toolchains — Matthew Collaro
item.description: Why exposing MBSE context through typed, governed operations beats dumping exported documents into a context window, and what the interface design has to get right.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: Deriving Safety Assessments From the Model Instead of Maintaining Them Beside It — Matthew Collaro
item.description: Hazard analyses go stale because they are maintained in parallel with the architecture. Generating them from the model changes which errors are possible.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: What I Learned Leading an MBSE Community of Practice — Matthew Collaro
item.description: Running a 100-engineer MBSE community of practice at Boeing taught me that modeling adoption fails for organizational reasons, and that the tool is almost never the problem.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: DoDAF and SysML on Defense Programs, Without the Viewpoint Theater — Matthew Collaro
item.description: DoDAF viewpoints get produced because they are deliverable, not because anyone reads them. Making them fall out of a coherent model is what turns compliance into engineering.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: Modeling Automotive HMI and Infotainment Integration — Matthew Collaro
item.description: Notification timing, media routing, and vehicle state synchronization defects are integration problems disguised as feature bugs. Behavioral modeling is how you find out which is which.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro

item.title: From the Factory Floor to Systems Architecture — Matthew Collaro
item.description: How writing overhaul instructions for flight control actuators turned out to be useful preparation for architecture modeling, and what I would tell someone making the same move.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Collaro
